There isn’t a single Mac or Linux clone of **PortableApps.com** at the same scale. The closest equivalents are different *mechanisms*, not one launcher + 1,400 repackaged apps.

## Linux: AppImage is the real parallel

**[AppImage](https://appimage.org/)** is the closest match to “drop a folder, run it, copy it to another machine”:

- One file (or a small folder), no root install
- Config often lives beside the app (`*.AppImage.home`, or `APPIMAGE` env)
- Copy to USB, another PC, or `~/Apps` and double-click (after `chmod +x`)
- Catalogs: [AppImageHub](https://www.appimagehub.com/), project GitHub releases, Flathub alternatives for some apps

Other Linux patterns that overlap with “portable”:

| Approach | Portable feel | Notes |
|----------|---------------|--------|
| **AppImage** | High | Nearest to PortableApps / XAMPP zip |
| **Static tarball** (Hugo, Node, Go binaries) | High | Unzip, add to `PATH`, move the tree |
| **Flatpak / Snap** | Medium | Installed into a store sandbox; not really a USB toolkit |
| **`.deb` / package manager** | Low | System integration, not “copy my desk” |

Many PortableApps staples have AppImage or tarball builds: **Firefox**, **LibreOffice**, **GIMP**, **VLC**, **Krita**, **Obsidian**, **VS Code** (official `.tar.gz`), etc.

## macOS: bundles are semi-portable; no unified platform

macOS doesn’t have a PortableApps.com-style ecosystem. What people actually do:

| Approach | Portable feel | Notes |
|----------|---------------|--------|
| **`.app` bundles** | Medium–high | Many apps are one folder in `/Applications`; drag-copy to another Mac often works |
| **Homebrew** (`brew install --prefix ~/homebrew`) | Medium | User-space install, not USB-first |
| **Official `.dmg` / `.zip` downloads** | Medium | Same idea as “portable zip” — extract and run |
| **MacPorts in a prefix** | Medium | Power-user, not beginner-friendly |

There’s no standard launcher + catalog like `Start.exe` on a stick. “Portable Mac apps” usually means **vendor ships a self-contained `.app`** you can copy.

## Cross-platform: the overlap from your draft

For the tools you already name in the post, the “equivalent” on Mac/Linux is often **the normal build**, not a special portable edition:

| Windows portable habit | Mac / Linux |
|------------------------|-------------|
| PortableApps **Firefox** | Regular Firefox (or tarball / AppImage on Linux) |
| **Notepad++** Portable | **Kate**, **Geany**, **VS Code/Cursor** — no Notepad++ on Mac/Linux |
| **LibreOffice** Portable | LibreOffice (`.dmg` / distro package / AppImage) |
| **GIMP** Portable | GIMP |
| **VLC** Portable | VLC |
| **Git** Portable | `git` via Homebrew, distro package, or static build |
| **XAMPP** portable | **MAMP** (Mac), **Laravel Valet**, **Docker**, or separate Apache/PHP/MySQL trees — messier, no one standard zip |

**Beyond Compare**, **Bitwarden**, **Brave/Chrome**, **Hugo**, **Node** — same story as in your draft: install once per OS, same workflow; not “one USB tree for all three.”

## The honest summary

- **Windows:** PortableApps.com = convention + launcher + catalog.
- **Linux:** **AppImage** (+ occasional static tarballs) = same *idea*, fragmented catalog.
- **macOS:** **Copyable `.app` bundles** + Homebrew = closest, but no shared standard.

If you’re expanding the draft, the punchline is probably: **portable on Windows was a workaround for installers and locked PCs; on Mac/Linux the OS already tolerates “app lives in a folder,” so the ecosystem never industrialized the way PortableApps did** — and **open-source cross-platform apps** fill most of the gap once you’re on three OSes.
